title: Insider-transaction cluster detection (buy/sell classification + time-windowed grouping)
description: Scoped out of backend-market-data-extra-fields (PR #183) and tracked via backend-market-data-extra-fields-followups's checklist: that task deliberately exposed `ExtendedData.insider_transactions` raw (yfinance's own `Insider`/`Position`/`Text`/`Shares`/`Value`/`Start Date`/`Ownership` fields, most-recent-first) with no buy/sell classification or time-windowed clustering computed, matching this codebase's established pattern of separating pattern/cluster *detection* from raw data *exposure* into its own later task (the direct precedent this task follows: backend-divergence-detection, backend-kangaroo-tail-pattern, and backend-support-resistance were each their own task after their underlying data/OHLCV was already available). Elder ch. 37 p. 147 (docs/ideas.md's own citation) treats a cluster of 3+ buys or sells by different insiders within a rolling month as a real, if secondary, signal -- worth noting alongside a stock's technical picture, not a standalone BUY/SELL trigger on its own (nothing in Analyse.md's confidence-scoring or Screen 1/2/3 rules currently references insider activity, and this task should not silently wire it into confidence scoring without that being its own explicit decision if ever proposed). The concrete new work needed, not yet done anywhere in this codebase: (1) `transaction_text`'s free text (e.g. 'Sale at price 220.00 - 225.00 per share.', 'Purchase at price 45.00 per share.') must be parsed into a buy/sell direction -- yfinance's own scraper doesn't provide a structured direction field, only this raw description, so this is squarely 'the book's concept is precise, the parsing mechanism is not' territory this task's own checklist should require a `decisions` entry for (which text patterns map to buy vs. sell vs. neither, e.g. option exercises/gifts/tax-withholding dispositions that aren't open-market conviction buys or sells the way Elder means); (2) a rolling time window and a 'same direction' grouping rule over `start_date` need a concrete, recorded definition (calendar month vs. 30 trading/calendar days; whether the 3+ must be distinct insiders or the count is per-filing regardless of insider identity -- Elder's own wording ('several insiders buying (or selling) within a one-month period', per docs/ideas.md's ch. 37 citation) leans toward requiring distinct insiders, but this should be an explicit, recorded call, not an unstated assumption); (3) where the resulting flag is exposed (extended_data itself, or a new sibling field) and how a consumer should read it (informational note vs. something a future confidence-scoring change could reference) needs to be decided and documented, consistent with the non-scope-creep precedent set by backend-market-data-extra-fields's own decision not to wire extended_data into any Screen/Impulse/Confidence computation. A frontend surface for this (e.g. a 'cluster detected' badge alongside the existing raw insider-transactions table added by frontend-fundamental-data-panel) is a natural, separate follow-up once this backend piece exists -- note it, but don't implement it as part of this task.

checklist.step: Decide and record the buy/sell classification rule for `transaction_text` (which literal patterns/keywords map to buy vs. sell vs. 'not a genuine open-market conviction transaction, exclude from clustering' -- e.g. option exercises, gifts, tax-withholding dispositions -- and how an unrecognized/unparseable text value is handled, e.g. excluded from clustering but still present in the raw list).

Decide and record the clustering window/threshold definition (rolling window length and units; whether the 3+ threshold requires distinct insiders or counts every qualifying filing; whether the window is anchored per-cluster or evaluated as a sliding window over the full available filing history).

Implement detection (new app/signals/ module, following the pattern of app.signals.divergence/kangaroo_tail/support_resistance) that classifies each transaction and flags qualifying buy clusters and sell clusters over the ticker's available insider_transactions history.

Tests with hand-computed reference cases: an unambiguous buy cluster, an unambiguous sell cluster, a mixed-direction set that does not cluster, fewer-than-threshold transactions within the window (no cluster), and at least one unparseable/excluded transaction-text case.

Decide and record where/how the result is exposed on GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis (extended_data vs. a new field) without wiring it into Screen/Impulse/Confidence/Portfolio-Risk computation unless that is itself made an explicit, separately-recorded decision; regenerate backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts; update docs/Analyse.md's existing 'Insider transactions' paragraph to reflect that clustering is now computed (and file/note the frontend-consumption follow-up rather than implementing it here).

decisions.decision: classify_transaction(transaction_text) maps text to "buy" only when it starts with "purchase" and "sell" only when it starts with "sale" (case/whitespace-insensitive), UNLESS the text contains any of a fixed exclusion-keyword list ("option", "exercise", "gift", "award", "grant", "tax", "conversion", "withholding") anywhere in it, in which case it's always "other" regardless of its leading word. Empty/whitespace-only text and any text that doesn't start with either leading word (after the exclusion check) is also "other".
decisions.rationale: yfinance's own transaction_text (this app already decided, in backend-market-data-extra-fields, to keep this raw rather than use yfinance's separate structured 'Transaction' column) is free text with no fixed vocabulary, but every genuine open-market buy/sell filing observed in this codebase's own test fixtures leads with exactly 'Purchase at price ...' or 'Sale at price ...'. The exclusion-keyword list targets the specific non-open-market dispositions this task's own description calls out by name (option exercises, gifts, tax-withholding dispositions) plus two more of the same character commonly seen in real insider filings (grants/awards of restricted stock, and derivative-security conversions) -- all of these can appear in text that still contains 'sale'/'purchase' vocabulary (e.g. yfinance's own 'Sale+Gift' composite descriptions, or 'Payment of exercise price ... by delivering or withholding shares'), so the exclusion check runs BEFORE the leading-word check, not after. Rejected: a purely leading-word-only rule with no exclusion list -- would misclassify a 'Sale+Gift'-style composite disposition as a genuine market sell, and Elder's own concept (insiders making a real market conviction bet) doesn't include an option exercise or a tax-driven forced sale, which reveal nothing about conviction. Rejected: an allowlist of exact known-good phrasings instead of a keyword-exclusion approach -- more brittle against yfinance's own text formatting drifting slightly over time (e.g. punctuation, price-range formatting), since it would silently reclassify as 'other' (safe, but silently losing real signal) rather than the chosen approach's silent-'other'-only-on-true-ambiguity behavior. An unrecognized/unparseable value (neither leading word) is 'other' -- excluded from clustering, but the raw InsiderTransaction is untouched and stays visible in extended_data.insider_transactions's raw list.

decisions.decision: A cluster requires 3+ DISTINCT insiders (by name) trading the same classified direction (buy or sell) within a rolling 30-CALENDAR-day window; the window is anchored at its own earliest qualifying transaction and clusters are found via a greedy, non-overlapping forward scan (extend the window from an anchor transaction while the next transaction is within 30 days of the anchor; if the resulting window reaches 3 distinct insiders, report it as a cluster and resume scanning strictly after it; otherwise advance the anchor by one transaction), not a continuously-sliding window. A transaction only counts toward a cluster if it has both a known insider name and a start_date -- one with either missing is excluded from clustering entirely (though untouched in the raw insider_transactions list) since it can never confirm or deny it's a genuinely DIFFERENT insider from the others.
decisions.rationale: Elder's own wording (docs/ideas.md's citation, ch. 37 p. 147) is 'several insiders buying (or selling) within a one-month period' -- 'several' is read as 3 (the smallest count 'several' can reasonably mean, and the exact number this task's own checklist/description asks for), and 'distinct insiders' (not just distinct filings) is the book's own emphasis on breadth of conviction across multiple people, not one person filing repeatedly. '30 calendar days' rather than a strict calendar-month boundary (1st-to-1st) was chosen because a strict calendar-month window would make a cluster's qualification an artifact of which day of the month the window happens to start on (three insiders buying Jan 28/Feb 2/Feb 5 span under 2 weeks but straddle a calendar-month boundary under a strict rule) -- a rolling 30-day window avoids that arbitrary edge effect and is the more natural reading of Elder's own 'within a one-month period' phrasing (a duration, not a specific calendar unit). An anchored, non-overlapping scan (rather than a continuously-sliding window that would report a new candidate cluster at every single-transaction shift) was chosen to avoid reporting many heavily-overlapping near-duplicate 'clusters' that are really the same underlying episode of insider activity -- matching the spirit of app.signals.support_resistance's own greedy sequential clustering (grouped once, not re-reported at every shift) even though the exact mechanics differ (time-windowed here vs. price-tolerance there). Rejected: counting every qualifying filing (not just distinct insiders) toward the 3+ threshold -- would let one insider's repeat filings alone trigger a 'cluster', directly contradicting Elder's own 'several insiders' (plural people) wording, which the task's own description flagged as the more likely correct reading. Rejected: a continuously-sliding window with a single 'most recent cluster' result (mirroring kangaroo_tail/divergence's single-most-recent-pattern shape) -- rejected because the task's own description explicitly asks for 'flags qualifying buy clusters and sell clusters' (plural, list-shaped, matching support_resistance_zones's own list-of-detections precedent), and multiple genuinely separate clustering episodes over a ticker's full filing history are real, useful, independent information, not noise to collapse into one.

decisions.decision: The result is exposed as a new top-level AnalysisResponse.insider_clusters: list[InsiderClusterOut] field (sibling to extended_data), not nested inside ExtendedDataOut, and computed directly in get_analysis from extended.insider_transactions (same compute-once-in-the-handler pattern as support_resistance_zones/profit_target) -- not folded into app.signals.engine.analyse()/analyse_history() and not added to GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators.
decisions.rationale: extended_data is this app's raw provider-facing exposure boundary (earnings/dividend dates, short interest, insider filings passed through close to yfinance's own shape); insider_clusters is a genuinely computed DETECTION result over that raw data, matching the established precedent that detection outputs -- support_resistance_zones, divergence, kangaroo_tail, profit_target -- are each their own top-level AnalysisResponse field rather than nested inside the raw data object they're derived from. Keeping it top-level also keeps ExtendedDataOut's own meaning stable (pure pass-through of what the provider reported) as a documentation/reasoning aid for future fields added to that object. Not added to GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators (the per-bar historical endpoint) because insider filings aren't a per-daily-bar concept the way indicators are -- there's one current cluster state per ticker, not one per historical bar, so there's no meaningful 'value as of this past bar' to backfill; this mirrors support_resistance_zones's own precedent of /analysis-only exposure (backend-support-resistance's decisions) for the same reason. Purely informational: NOT wired into signal/confidence_breakdown/screens/portfolio risk anywhere -- matches every other detection field's own non-scope-creep precedent, verified via grep (no reference to insider_clusters/InsiderCluster anywhere in app/signals/confidence.py, app/signals/triple_screen.py, app/signals/impulse.py, or app/portfolio/risk.py).
